docs.title: academicflow
docs.text:
Write, check, cite and export scientific papers without leaving Jupyter.

pip install academicflow

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Text analysis: word count, reading time, readability grade, keywords, passive voice.
  • Style checker: informal language, repeated phrases, and section-aware rules such as tense in Methods and abstract length.
  • Terminology consistency: catches "data set" vs "dataset" and undefined acronyms across the whole paper.
  • Venue profiles: apa, ieee and nature presets control citation format, word limits and style rules together.
  • Citations: load a .bib file, write [@key], and get APA, IEEE or Nature formatting, plus checks for missing keys and duplicate DOIs.
  • Abstract generator: extractive by default, with an optional LLM backend.
  • Export: one command to .docx or .tex, with references already formatted.

docs.title: How it differs from existing tools
docs.text: Tool Does academicflow adds textstat Readability scores Section-aware rules, notebook integration proselint Generic prose linting Academic and venue-specific rules, cross-section terminology pybtex BibTeX parsing Inline citation rendering in notebooks, integrity checks nbconvert Notebook conversion Paper-structured export with formatted references

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install academicflow

Optional extras: pip install "academicflow[llm]" for LLM abstracts, "academicflow[nlp]" for spaCy-based analysis.

docs.title: Five-minute tour
docs.text:
%load_ext academicflow
%acite refs.bib

%%academic --style=apa --section=introduction
Large language models have changed NLP [@vaswani2017].

%astats
%acheck
%aabstract
%aexport paper.docx

docs.title: Abstract generator (academicflow.summarize)
docs.text: Generate a summary of any text, or a full abstract from a paper's sections. The default method is extractive TextRank: it runs offline, needs no API key and gives the same result every time. An optional LLM backend writes new sentences instead, and falls back to TextRank automatically if anything goes wrong.

docs.title: In a notebook
docs.text:
%load_ext academicflow

%%academic --section=introduction
...

%aabstract              # TextRank abstract, 200 words
%aabstract --words=150  # shorter
%aabstract --llm        # LLM abstract (see configuration below)

docs.title: From Python
docs.text:
from academicflow.summarize import summarize, generate_abstract

summarize(long_text, max_words=100)

generate_abstract({
    "1. Introduction": "...",
    "2. Materials and Methods": "...",
    "Results": "...",
    "Conclusion": "...",
}, max_words=200)

docs.title: How the extractive method works
docs.text:
1. The text is split into sentences, and each sentence becomes a TF-IDF vector (stopwords removed).
  2. Sentences are linked by cosine similarity, and PageRank scores how central each sentence is.
  3. Sentences in the first or last 20% of the text get a small boost (×1.15), as do sentences containing the text's top keywords (×1.10).
  4. The best sentences that fit in max_words are returned in their original order.

generate_abstract is section-aware. It takes up to two of the best sentences from the introduction, methods, results and conclusion, in that order, and shares the word budget between the sections that exist. Section names are normalised:

You write Treated as Introduction, Background, Motivation introduction Methods, Methodology, Materials and Methods, Approach, Experiments methods Results, Evaluation, Findings results Conclusion, Discussion, Summary, Future work conclusion

Numbering such as 2. or III. is ignored, and any existing Abstract section is skipped. If none of the four standard sections exist, the whole text is summarised.

docs.title: LLM backend (optional)
docs.text:
pip install "academicflow[llm]"

Any OpenAI-compatible API works. Configure it with environment variables or with arguments (model=, base_url=, api_key=):

Variable Meaning Example ACADEMICFLOW_LLM_MODEL Model name (required) llama3.2 ACADEMICFLOW_LLM_BASE_URL API URL; leave unset for OpenAI http://localhost:11434/v1 OPENAI_API_KEY API key; not needed for local servers

Local and free, with Ollama:

ollama pull llama3.2
export ACADEMICFLOW_LLM_MODEL=llama3.2
export ACADEMICFLOW_LLM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1

summarize(text, method="llm")
generate_abstract(sections, method="llm")

The model is told to use only facts from the text and never to invent results or citations. Answers longer than max_words are cut at a sentence boundary.

If the openai package, the model name or the key is missing, or the request fails, you get one warning and the TextRank result instead, so a demo never breaks.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Extractive summaries reuse the author's sentences, so they can read less smoothly than a hand-written abstract.
  • Sentence splitting quality depends on academicflow.core.split_sentences.
  • LLM output should always be checked by the authors before submission.
